package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of struts2-core contain a critical vulnerability in the HttpParameters class that allows remote code execution (RCE) due to improper case handling. This enables attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected servers, making the package highly dangerous in its vulnerable versions.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Improper case-insensitive handling of HTTP parameters allows attackers to bypass security checks and inject malicious input, which can be executed as code on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code fails to properly validate and sanitize user-supplied HTTP parameters, allowing attackers to craft requests that bypass intended security controls and trigger code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would strictly validate and sanitize all user input, especially in web frameworks. The actual behavior allows user input to be executed as code, violating core security principles.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Case-insensitive parameter handling is sometimes used for user convenience, but never for security-sensitive operations or code execution.
key_indicators: direct execution of user-supplied parameter values
lack of input sanitization or validation

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a specially formed HTTP request with parameter names exploiting case-insensitive handling.
attack_chain.leads_to: Bypass of security checks and injection of malicious input.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable HttpParameters class processes the malicious parameter and executes the attacker's payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains control of the server, potentially leading to data theft, lateral movement, or further compromise.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise or data exfiltration.

behavioral_signatures: Unusual HTTP requests with parameter names differing only in case
Execution of unexpected processes or commands triggered by HTTP input
Unexpected code execution paths in web application logs
file_indicators: References to org.apache.struts2.dispatcher.HttpParameters in stack traces or logs
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP requests with suspicious or malformed parameters
Outbound connections initiated by the web server process following suspicious requests
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for HTTP requests with parameter names that differ only in case, especially those targeting .action endpoints. Scan for the presence of vulnerable struts2-core versions in your software inventory. Review application logs for evidence of unexpected code execution or process spawning following HTTP requests. Use web application firewalls (WAFs) to block suspicious parameter patterns and employ runtime application self-protection (RASP) to detect and prevent exploitation attempts.
